verdict.rationale: Cloudflare states directly that it bills only for compute, not wall time, including during long agent workflows and hibernating WebSockets. The Agents SDK docs add that hibernating agents cost nothing when inactive, which matches the story's core ask. missing for 10: detailed pricing documentation (CPU-time billing units, rates, how waiting on I/O or subrequests is treated), independent or hands-on corroboration of actual billing behavior.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can pay only for active compute time rather than idle wall-clock time

citations.quote: Cloudflare charges only for compute, not wall time, even during long agent workflows or hibernating WebSockets.
Agents hibernate when idle and wake on demand. You can run millions of them — one per user, per session, per game room — each costs nothing when inactive.
